mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a modular and stick-built tiny home ADU for multigenerational living?

acceptedAnswer.text: A modular tiny home ADU is constructed off-site in a factory setting in sections, then transported and assembled on your property. This often leads to faster construction times and controlled quality due to the indoor environment. A stick-built tiny home ADU, conversely, is constructed entirely on your property from the ground up, similar to a traditional home. Stick-built offers greater flexibility in design and customization. The choice depends on your budget, timeline, and desired level of customization for your multigenerational living space.
acceptedAnswer.description: Modular tiny home ADUs are built off-site and assembled, often faster. Stick-built ADUs are constructed on-site, offering more design flexibility. The best choice depends on budget and customization needs.
